subtitle: Where Timber, Coir and Monsoon Memory Become Ships

panels.shot: epic aerial wide over Beypore estuary at sunset
panels.action: The wide mouth of the Chaliyar river meets the Arabian Sea, dotted with half-built wooden hulls along Beypore’s shore as tiny figures of shipwrights move like ants around giants of timber.

dialogue.text: For centuries at Beypore, unnamed shipwrights stitched wood and coir into mighty urus that carried the Zamorin’s world across the sea—yet their science lived only from hand to hand, never on paper.

i18n.hi: सदियों से बेपोर में गुमनाम कारीगरों ने लकड़ी और कय्या से ऐसे उरु सिले जो ज़मोरिन की दुनिया समंदर पार ले गए — पर उनकी विद्या बस हाथों में रही, कागज़ पर नहीं।

panels.shot: low-angle wide from riverbank, framing half-built uru hull towering over workers
panels.action: A Beypore Shipwright stands on a scaffolding plank, surveying the curved ribs of a massive hull rising from the sandy yard beside the Chaliyar, while other craftsmen bend over timbers below.

dialogue.text: Ibn Battuta wrote of Calicut’s crowded harbor and strong ships. Few lines mention Beypore by name, but his words hang over this river mouth, where those ships were born in timber and sweat.

i18n.hi: इब्न बतूता ने कालीकट की भरी बंदरगाह और मज़बूत जहाज़ों का ज़िक्र किया। बेपोर का नाम कम ही आया, पर उसकी बातें आज भी इस मुहाने पर तैरती हैं, जहाँ वो जहाज़ लकड़ी और पसीने से जनमे थे।

panels.shot: close-up on weathered hands sketching hull curves in wet sand with a stick
panels.action: The Beypore Shipwright crouches, drawing a sweeping hull outline in damp sand, his hands calloused and steady, as apprentices watch the emerging geometry in silent focus.

dialogue.text: Here there were no printed plans. Hulls began as lines in sand, as memory in muscle—ratios of length, beam and draft carried in a master’s eye, tested by monsoon after monsoon.

i18n.hi: ये लोग नक्शे नहीं छापते थे। ज्योंत रेत पर लकीरों से शुरू होती, माँसपेशियों की याद से — लंबाई, चौड़ाई, गहराई के हिसाब उस्ताद की आँख में, हर मानसून की कसौटी पर खरे।

panels.shot: medium shot of shipwright selecting a teak log from a pile, sunlight catching grain
panels.action: The Beypore Shipwright grips a great teak log, inspecting its straight grain and slight curve, while other logs of teak and anjili lie stacked under a palm-fringed sky.

dialogue.text: Teak from inland forests and anjili from Kerala’s hills arrived by river and cart. Each log was weighed by eye for strength and bend, matched to a place in a future hull.

i18n.hi: भीतर के जंगलों से सागौन, और केरल की पहाड़ियों से अंजीली नदी और बैलगाड़ियों पर आती। हर लट्ठा आँख से तौला जाता, ताकत और मोड़ के लिए, किसी आने वाले ज्योंत की सही जगह के लिए।

panels.shot: tight close-up of adze striking wood, curving a rib against simple wooden template
panels.action: With focused eyes, the Beypore Shipwright swings an adze, shaving a rib to match a curved wooden template, fine curls of teak falling onto packed earth.

dialogue.text: Ribs were not guessed. Templates, rules of thumb and long practice gave each frame its arc, so that dozens of pieces of timber could agree on one smooth, sea-cutting curve.

i18n.hi: पसलीं अंदाज़े से नहीं बनतीं। साँचे, अनुभवी नियम और सालों की रियाज़ हर फ्रेम को उसका कमान देते, ताकि दर्जनों टुकड़े मिलकर एक चिकनी, लहर चीरती वक्र बना सकें।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of half-framed hull, ribs rising like a wooden skeleton
panels.action: Inside the growing hull, the Beypore Shipwright stands among rising ribs that form a skeletal tunnel, measuring spacing with a rope, apprentices holding the line taut.

dialogue.text: The shipwrights knew the Chaliyar’s moods and the Arabian Sea’s long swell. The hull’s deep belly and high prow were tuned to ride cargo-heavy yet answer the pull of monsoon winds.

i18n.hi: कारीगरों को चेलियार का मिज़ाज और अरब सागर की लंबी लहरें पता थीं। जहाज़ का गहरा पेट और ऊँचा नाक माल-भरे सफ़र के लिए तराशा जाता, फिर भी मानसून की हवा का खिंचाव सुन सके।

panels.shot: close-up on coir rope being twisted and passed through plank edge holes
panels.action: The Beypore Shipwright threads thick coir rope through bored holes in two plank edges, apprentices pulling the lashings tight as the planks draw together.

dialogue.text: Coir, spun from coconut husk, was their hidden steel. Twisted and passed through holes in planks, it let the hull flex with the sea instead of cracking against it.

i18n.hi: नारियल की जटा से सूत बना कय्या उनका छुपा लोहा था। तख्तों में छेदों से गुज़ारकर और कसकर, वो ज्योंत को समंदर के साथ झुकने देता, उससे टूटने नहीं देता।

panels.shot: medium shot from deck level, shipwright inspecting sewn seams and some metal fastenings
panels.action: Standing on a plank edge, the Beypore Shipwright runs his hand along a seam of sewn planks, where coir lashings sit beside a few metal fastenings in the frame.

dialogue.text: Earlier urus leaned heavily on sewn planks; later ones mixed coir lashings with metal fastenings. The craft shifted with markets, yet kept its core: flexible, repairable hulls for hard seas.

i18n.hi: पुराने उरु तख्तों की सिलाई पर ज़्यादा टिके थे; बाद के उरु में कय्या की बंधन के साथ लोहे की जकड़ भी आई। हुनर बाज़ार के साथ बदला, पर असल बात रही — सख़्त समंदर के लिए लचीली, सुधरने वाली ज्योंतें।

panels.shot: close-up of caulker pressing fibre into seam, black pitch smeared over
panels.action: Kneeling beside the hull, the Beypore Shipwright pushes fibre into a narrow seam, then smooths dark pitch over it, his face intent, the timber gleaming in patches.

dialogue.text: Every seam was packed with fibre and sealed with pitch. Between river water, salt spray and heat, a uru survived only if its skin stayed tight. Caulking was quiet, exacting science.

i18n.hi: हर जोड़ में रेशे ठूँसे जाते, ऊपर राल जड़ी जाती। नदी का पानी, नमकीन छींटे और धूप के बीच, उरु तभी बचता था जब उसकी चमड़ी कसी रहे। गूंजन एक खामोश, सटीक विज्ञान था।

panels.shot: wide shot of busy yard with two different vessels: a large trading uru and a smaller, sleeker coastal craft
panels.action: The Beypore Shipwright stands between a massive cargo hull and a smaller, sleeker coastal boat, gesturing to younger men as they compare their lines and proportions.

dialogue.text: Around Calicut, François Pyrard saw big ocean traders and swift coastal craft. The Kunjali Marakkars’ paraos and fustas drew on the same skills, shaped for speed and maneuver instead of bulk.

i18n.hi: कालीकट के आसपास फ्राँस्वा पिरार ने बड़े समुद्री सौदागर और फुर्तीले तटवर्ती जहाज़ देखे। कुंजाली मरक्कारों के पराओ और फुस्ता भी इसी हुनर से बने, भारीपन नहीं, रफ़्तार और चालाकी के लिए।

panels.shot: medium shot of shipwright and Arab merchant on riverside, pointing at hull and horizon
panels.action: On the riverbank, the Beypore Shipwright speaks with a robed Arab merchant; both point from the finished hull toward the hazy line of the Arabian Sea.

dialogue.text: Logan’s Malabar Manual notes Beypore’s tie to Calicut’s trade. Arab merchants trusted these yards, ordering urus to sail to Hormuz, Basra, and later the Gulf ports, carrying spices, timber and people.

i18n.hi: लोगन की ‘मालाबार मैन्युअल’ में बेपोर का कालीकट की मंडी से रिश्ता दर्ज है। अरब सौदागर इन घाटों पर भरोसा करते, उरु बनवाते जो होर्मुज़, बसरा और बाद में खाड़ी के बंदरगाहों तक जाते, मसाले, लकड़ी और लोग ले जाते।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of hull being launched, crowd straining on ropes as it slides to water
panels.action: The Beypore Shipwright leads men hauling thick ropes as the huge uru hull slowly slides down greased logs toward the shimmering river, villagers watching from the banks.

dialogue.text: Hold steady! Let her feel the water, not fear it.

i18n.hi: थाम कर रखो! उसे पानी को महसूस करने दो, डरने मत दो।

panels.shot: wide shot of newly launched uru floating on river, shipwright’s reflection in water
panels.action: The newly launched uru sits low and stable on the Chaliyar, its tall prow mirrored in the river, as the Beypore Shipwright stands at the bank, his reflection touching the ship’s shadow.

dialogue.text: Launches tested years of judgment. If the hull sat wrong, it betrayed every choice of timber and curve. If it rode true, the river itself confirmed the master’s stored calculations.

i18n.hi: हर ज्योंत की पहली नाव-परीक्षा सालों की सोच की कसौटी थी। ज्योंत अगर गलत बैठती, तो हर लकड़ी, हर वक्र की चुगली कर देती। सही तैरती, तो नदी खुद उस्ताद की गिनी-चुनी गणना मान लेती।

panels.shot: interior deck shot, shipwright teaching a young apprentice to knot coir and read grain
panels.action: On the deck of a moored uru, the Beypore Shipwright guides an apprentice’s hands as they twist coir and tap a plank to read its sound, the river gliding past.

dialogue.text: Knowledge stayed alive by touch. Masters taught apprentices how wood should sound under a tap, how coir should feel when tight enough, how a hull should lean under a crosswind.

i18n.hi: विद्या छूकर ज़िंदा रहती थी। उस्ताद शागिर्दों को सिखाते कि चोट पर लकड़ी कैसी आवाज़ दे, कसने पर कय्या कैसा हाथ में लगे, और आड़ी हवा पर ज्योंत कैसे झुके।

panels.shot: split-scene wide: one side shows older medieval yard, the other modern yard with power tools, same river
panels.action: A composite view shows an earlier Beypore yard with hand tools and bare-chested workers on one side, and a modern yard with power tools and safety gear on the other, both along the Chaliyar.

dialogue.text: Himanshu Prabha Ray and Kerala archaeologists trace this coast’s long maritime life. Methods and markets changed, but Beypore stayed a place where timber met ocean routes and local skill met global demand.

i18n.hi: हिमांशु प्रभा राय और केरल के पुरातत्ववेत्ता इस तट की लंबी समुद्री कहानी खोज रहे हैं। तरीक़े और बाज़ार बदले, पर बेपोर वही जगह रहा जहाँ लकड़ी समुद्री राहों से मिली और स्थानीय हुनर दुनिया की माँग से।

panels.shot: wide shot of uru heading out to sea, shipwright watching from shore with apprentices
panels.action: From the sandy shore, the Beypore Shipwright and his apprentices watch an uru under sail, shrinking as it moves toward the open Arabian Sea at dawn.

dialogue.text: Our work will touch lands we will never see.

i18n.hi: हमारा काम उन ज़मीनों को छुएगा जिन्हें हम कभी नहीं देखेंगे।

panels.shot: close-up on the face of an elderly shipwright beside a younger one, river behind them
panels.action: An elderly Beypore Shipwright sits by the river, lines of age marking his face, as a younger shipwright listens and watches his hands trace the curve of an imaginary hull in the air.

dialogue.text: Some compare these sewn hulls to far older ships of distant lands, but links are debated. What is certain is this: Beypore’s urus endure because each generation makes the next a witness and a partner.

i18n.hi: कुछ लोग इन सिले हुए ढाँचों को दूर देशों के प्राचीन जहाज़ों से जोड़ते हैं, पर रिश्तों पर मतभेद हैं। पक्की बात बस इतनी है — बेपोर के उरु इसलिए टिके रहे, क्योंकि हर नई पीढ़ी अगली को गवाह और साथी बनाती रही।

panels.shot: epic aerial over Beypore and sea lanes, faint silhouettes of urus across centuries
panels.action: From high above, the Chaliyar estuary, Beypore yards and the open sea stretch out, faint layered silhouettes of urus from different eras tracing imagined routes toward Arabia and beyond.

dialogue.text: The Beypore shipwrights never wrote treatises, yet their hulls carried Malabar’s power, trade and resistance. Their true invention was a living chain of minds where technology survived because hands kept teaching hands.

i18n.hi: बेपोर के कारीगरों ने कभी किताबें नहीं लिखीं, पर उनकी ज्योंतों ने मालाबार की ताकत, व्यापार और बग़ावत ढोई। उनकी असली खोज एक ज़िंदा ज़ंजीर थी, जहाँ तकनीक बची, क्योंकि हाथ हमेशा हाथों को सिखाते रहे।

title_i18n.en: Beypore Uru Builders Stitch the Sea
title_i18n.hi: बेपोर के उरु कारीगर समंदर को सिलते हैं

subtitle_i18n.en: Where Timber, Coir and Monsoon Memory Become Ships
subtitle_i18n.hi: जहाँ लकड़ी, कय्या और मानसून की याद जहाज़ बन जाती है
